synopsis: Resources Safety and Health Queensland (RSHQ) publishes QGN 27 on collision prevention (2017) and QGN 33 on autonomous mobile machinery [f15541]. QGN 27 reports that collisions accounted for 26% of mineral mine and quarry fatalities between 1998 and 2016, while a separate RSHQ alert recorded 48 mobile-equipment collisions and near misses at open-cut coal mines from 1 January to 27 May 2017 [f3103, f3106]. QGN 27 identifies vehicle-to-vehicle, vehicle-to-person and vehicle-to-infrastructure interactions as important high-potential incident classes, including a worked scenario of a loader striking a pedestrian on a roadway [f3104, f3105]. Secondary reporting of RSHQ's July 2024 Quarterly Report indicates that mobile plant collisions remained among the leading high-potential incidents and that the Deputy Chief Inspector was particularly concerned about reliance on “positive communication” as the primary control; these later findings are presented through secondary reporting rather than directly from the report [f3109, f3110].

relations.note: Adds QGN 27's historical collision-fatality statistic to the glossary's publication listing.
Specifies the collision interaction classes covered by QGN 27.
Provides a worked example of the vehicle-to-person incident class.
Adds a specific control concern to the report's continuing collision-risk finding.
